_readme: Autonomous: the harness auto-joins a fake client, force-ends each round at
40 minutes and restarts the map. Sol and Centauri run VANILLA AI; the alien
runs Si_RTS_AI. Combat is ON, which is the whole point — this is the first
night the military layer issues orders against an opponent that shoots back.
TWO PREFERENCES MUST ALSO BE SET, and they live in MelonPreferences.cfg
because they are vanilla/harness settings rather than ours. Edit only while
the server is STOPPED — MelonLoader rewrites that file from memory on
shutdown and reverts anything changed while it runs:
EnemyBroke is the dangerous one. It zeroes human cash and purges their
starter units every second while testMode is true, so leaving it on would
have produced a night of rounds with no vanilla AI to fight and a log that
_soak: testMode true — auto-join, force-end, map restart.
suppressCombat FALSE — it is gated on testMode, so the soak default would
have silenced every attack order in the game. This is the line that makes
tonight a combat test rather than another eco run.
endRoundAfterMinutes 40 — long enough for the push trigger to have a chance:
it needs a full 120s army-growth window, banked cash, and a discovered
enemy structure before it will commit to anything.
roundsPerMap 24 — one map all night. Combat variance is already large, so
holding the ground constant is what makes two rounds comparable at all.
storageBufferCaches 0 — a measurement scaffold, and with combat on it is
also a hundred free structures parked next to the Nest for the enemy.
_configCycle: ARMS ARE OFF TONIGHT, deliberately, and this is the one place I would push
The producer-density arms measure income at 25 minutes. With combat on, how
much a round earns is dominated by whether the enemy walked into the base at
minute 18 — variance that swamps a producer-density difference the two clean
soaks could not separate anyway (2026-08-06: every arm inside +/-6%). Twelve
rounds a night at 40 minutes is far too few to pull it back out.
The military layer has meanwhile NEVER completed a round issuing orders
against an opponent that fights. The first question is not which ratio wins,
it is whether the thing behaves — and that question wants one configuration
repeated, so a bad round is a bad round rather than a bad arm.
To run arms anyway it is one line: put back
_military: Everything on. This is bring-up steps 2 and 3 at once, which is not the order
the docs recommend — but a soak can afford to look silly and a played game
cannot, and offence is the least measured code in the mod.
WHAT TO READ IN THE MORNING, in order:
1. combat.jsonl rows with "sides":2 — the first two-sided engagements this
project has ever recorded. Everything about pricing calibrates off them.
Rows are tagged with the mission kind that owned the ground, so exchange
ratios can be read per kind: garrison vs defend vs push.
2. [MISSION] posture lines. Did it ever push? Against what estimate? If
'theirs~0' all night, the enemy-value field is not seeing anything and
the push guard is doing its job for the wrong reason.
3. [BATTALION] — do defend battalions get units now, or is the garrison
still taking everything? That was the round-one defect.
4. [PLAN/EXEC] REPAIR vs REPAIR BLOCKED. Repair fired zero times out of 22
5. Alien structures lost, in the round summary. 70 lost of 125 built was
_lockAlienCommander: Harmless here — the fake client joins a human team and never takes the alien
seat. Left on so the soak runs the same configuration as the played game.
_eco: The tuned economy, unchanged, so tonight only adds combat as a variable.
